title: Few-shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection via Dynamic Intra-modal Sparsity Attention and Quality-aware Cross-modal Fusion in Microservice System

problem.claim: Microservice architectures require robust few-shot anomaly detection to prevent cascading failures.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal approaches are inadequate for cold-start scenarios because they depend on extensive training data and struggle with intra-modal feature extraction and heterogeneous multimodal alignment.

contributions.claim: FuseGuard uses modality-specific feature extraction mechanisms for metrics, traces, and logs to adaptively represent time-evolving patterns.
FuseGuard performs hierarchical cross-modal alignment through token projection, layer-wise distillation, and consistency learning while preserving modality-specific features.
FuseGuard dynamically weights modalities using uncertainty estimation for quality-aware multimodal fusion.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluation on three open-source platforms and one production system.
The authors report that FuseGuard outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 19.69%–77.07% F1-score across four datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Robust few-shot anomaly detection is needed for dynamic microservice architectures.
Existing multimodal approaches are limited in cold-start settings and face feature-extraction and cross-modal-alignment challenges.
FuseGuard combines dynamic intra-modal feature extraction, hierarchical cross-modal alignment, and uncertainty-based quality-aware fusion.
The authors report evaluation across four datasets, including open-source platforms and a production system, with higher reported F1-score than SOTA.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates intra-modal representation learning from cross-modal alignment and fusion.

interpretation.claim: A staged multimodal design may help preserve modality-specific information while enabling cross-modal transfer.

application.claim: For few-shot multimodal monitoring, consider modality-specific encoders followed by alignment and uncertainty-aware fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition is effective outside the reported anomaly-detection settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, few-shot protocols, baselines, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance.
